title: Smallest Sufficient Team
summary: Given a list of required skills and a list of people, each with their respective skills, find a sufficient team of the smallest possible size such that every required skill is covered by at least one person in the team.
statement: Given a list of required skills and a list of people, each with their respective skills, find a sufficient team of the smallest possible size such that every required skill is covered by at least one person in the team. Return the indices of the people who form this sufficient team.
constraints: All required skills can be covered.
Return the indices of a minimum-size sufficient team in any order.
hints: Encode required skills as bits and map each person to a mask.
For every current covered mask, consider adding the next person.
Keep the candidate with smallest (team length,index tuple) for each combined mask.
Dominated larger teams can never improve a future union, while tie ordering makes output deterministic.
editorial: Dominated larger teams can never improve a future union, while tie ordering makes output deterministic.

tests.explanation: People zero and two form the unique smallest team.
People one and two cover all six skills with minimum size two.
